scope: Bounded primary-source literature review for gauge-invariant physical-shell response; no exhaustive search or novelty claim.

sources.title: First and Second Order Perturbations of Hypersurfaces
sources.access: full experimental HTML; metadata independently inspected
sources.short_excerpt: Let Tε be a C² one-parameter family of covariant tensor fields
sources.finding: The derivative of a moving-embedding pullback is the pullback of the field derivative plus its Lie derivative along the embedding velocity.
sources.conditions: C² fields and C² family of embeddings; differentiable-manifold framework. This is a geometric identity and supplies no evolution or response nonvanishing theorem.
sources.hdblast_use: Directly supports including the embedding term in the physical shell scalar tangent; fixing the shell sets that term to zero only in that chosen gauge.

sources.title: Perturbation of junction condition and doubly gauge-invariant variables
sources.access: full experimental HTML; canonical abstract page separately retrieved
sources.finding: Bulk coordinate gauge changes and intrinsic hypersurface reparameterizations are independent. Induced metric/extrinsic curvature and junction perturbations require the embedding perturbation.
sources.conditions: General linear perturbative junction geometry, then constant-curvature spatial symmetry for harmonic doubly invariant variables. No compact-profile response theorem.
sources.hdblast_use: Supports the distinction between physical shell pullback and a coordinate value at fixed y, and checking both spacetime and shell gauge freedom.
sources.date_caution: Experimental HTML includes a spurious-looking August 24, 2026 heading; canonical abs page gives submission 19 June 2000 and revision 20 October 2000. Use canonical metadata.

sources.title: Brane World Cosmology — Gauge-Invariant Formalism for Perturbation
sources.locator: Section III.3.3, Section IV.2.3 equations (151)–(153), and Section V
sources.short_excerpt: the boundary condition is dependent on the type of the intrinsic matter perturbation
sources.finding: General gauge-invariant bulk/junction framework; scalar reduction to the cited single master equation uses a vacuum background with constant-curvature two-dimensional orbit space.
sources.conditions: The general equations allow bulk matter, but the particular scalar master reduction retrieved does not cover a generic nonconstant bulk scalar.
sources.hdblast_use: Methodological comparison for a coupled scalar/metric shell calculation; do not substitute its vacuum master equation for HDBLAST's nonconstant bulk Einstein–scalar system.

sources.title: Wave equation with Robin condition, quantitative estimates of strong unique continuation at the boundary
sources.access: five targeted in-body passages including Theorem 2.1
sources.short_excerpt: Let A(x) be a real-valued symmetric n × n
sources.finding: Quantitative strong continuation for the boundary trace of a scalar wave satisfying a homogeneous Robin law.
sources.conditions: Time-independent symmetric uniformly elliptic Lipschitz A(x), Lipschitz Robin coefficient, C^{1,1} local boundary, scalar equation and stated time/regularity scales. The theorem controls continuation of the boundary trace; it is not a universal finite-time observation theorem for a coupled system.
sources.hdblast_use: Possible model for a future scalar-specific continuation argument only after checking the time-dependent warped coefficients, metric coupling, and boundary operator.

sources.title: Approximate boundary synchronization by groups for a coupled system of wave equations with coupled Robin boundary conditions
sources.access: full experimental HTML and canonical metadata inspection
sources.short_excerpt: is not a standard type of Holmgren’s uniqueness theorem
sources.finding: Invariant subspaces in the observation kernel cause invisible solutions. Full composite coupling rank is necessary; the paper explicitly declines to make it a general sufficient condition for incomplete Robin boundary observation.
sources.conditions: Bounded smooth Euclidean domain, constant finite matrices A and B, scalar Laplacian common principal part, separated Dirichlet and Robin boundary portions; B is symmetric or similar to symmetric in the applicable well-posedness framework.
sources.hdblast_use: Rules out an unsupported leap from 'nonzero bulk tangent' or a rank check alone to 'nonzero observed shell scalar'. Full coupled observation or a constructive profile calculation is needed.
sources.date_caution: Experimental HTML date heading differs from canonical 2022 arXiv metadata; cite the identifier and canonical metadata.

sources.title: Brane Cosmology from AdS/BCFT
sources.access: full experimental HTML and canonical metadata inspection
sources.short_excerpt: though the bulk gravity is the pure gravity
sources.finding: Constructs scalar-bearing EOW-brane cosmological toy models, mainly in AdS3, including big-bang-like solutions for suitable brane potentials.
sources.conditions: Scalar field localized on the brane; pure gravity in the bulk; different dimensional and holographic setup from HDBLAST.
sources.hdblast_use: A current related brane-cosmology comparison, not evidence or a theorem validating HDBLAST's bulk-scalar shell or our Universe's origin.

sources.title: Exact boundary controllability for one-dimensional wave equations systems with a time dependent potential in non-cylindrical domains
sources.access: publisher abstract, introduction and beginning of setup; full later theorem body not retrieved
sources.short_excerpt: nullity after a suitable instant of time
sources.finding: Recent exact controllability via HUM for scalar and coupled one-dimensional wave equations with time-dependent potential and moving endpoint.
sources.conditions: One space dimension, endpoint speed below characteristic speed, potential depends only on time and is smooth/bounded/eventually zero, Dirichlet control on the moving endpoint. Later exact theorem assumptions have not been fully audited.
sources.hdblast_use: Useful recent moving-boundary method comparison; its hypotheses and control/observation operator do not directly match a fixed-shell coupled Robin Einstein–scalar problem.

sources.title: Uniqueness theorem for a coupled system of wave equations with incomplete internal observation and application to approximate controllability
sources.access: publisher metadata and abstract only; paper-index full text unavailable
sources.finding: Abstract states a necessary and sufficient Kalman rank condition for its incomplete internal observation system.
sources.conditions: Internal observation is different from Robin boundary observation. Full body assumptions were not retrieved or audited.
sources.hdblast_use: Excluded as a direct sufficiency citation; do not conflate this internal result with the distinct Robin-boundary paper.

retrieval_limitations: Experimental HTML can duplicate mathematical notation and insert noncanonical date headings; use arXiv canonical metadata and cited equation labels.
Targeted in-body passage retrieval is not a complete paper audit.
Two recent examples are method comparisons with different scalar location, dimension, principal coefficients, or boundary operator.
No retrieved theorem has been established to imply a nonzero HDBLAST physical shell response.
